Rashi on Nazir 18a:10:1.english: What is the reason of Rabbi - Who said [that] the naziriteship of purity does not take effect upon him until the day of bringing his offerings.

Rashi on Nazir 18a:10:2.hebrew: דאמר קרא וכפר עליו מאשר חטא על הנפש וגו' - דמשמע: אימתי "וקדש את ראשו" שיתחיל למנות? בו בזמן שכיפר עליו, דהיינו בשמיני:
Rashi on Nazir 18a:10:2.english: As the verse states: “And make atonement for him, for he sinned by the soul,” etc. - Which implies: When is “and he shall sanctify his head,” [meaning] that he begins to count? At the time that [the priest] atoned for him, that is, on the eighth [day].

Rashi on Nazir 18a:1:1.hebrew: דאי סלקא דעתך תגלחת טומאה ימי חלוטו מי לא בעי תגלחת - והכתיב: "וכבס המטהר את בגדיו" וגו', וההוא דינא דקא מייתי: "ומה נזיר בקבר כו'" — היכי קאתי? והא זה וזה ראויין לתגלחת! לעולם אימא לך: תגלחת דטומאה, כיון שהוזה ושנה וטבל, מתגלח בשביעי שלו. והאי דקא פריך "ימי חלוטו שאין שערו ראוי לתגלחת" — בתגלחת דנזירות קאמר: דאילו נזירות בקבר, כשהוא מגלח מעכשיו, מתגלח על נזירות; אבל נזיר מצורע, כשמתגלח תחילה, מתגלח על שנתרפא מצרעתו. והכי קתני: ימי חלוטו שאין ראוי לתגלחת טומאה דנזיר אלא לתגלחת דצרעת, לא כל שכן שאין עולין מן המנין דנזירות דטהרה? ולעולם אימא לך: היכא דנזר והוא בבית הקברות, טעון גילוח דטומאה:
Rashi on Nazir 18a:1:1.english: For if it should enter your mind [that the baraita refers to] the shaving of impurity, does [a leper at the end of] his days of confirmed [leprosy] not require shaving? - And is it not written: “And he who is to be cleansed shall wash his clothes [and shave off all his hair]...” (Leviticus 14:8)? And that logical argument which [the baraita] adduced: “Just as a nazirite in a cemetery, etc.” — how does it follow? Behold, both this one and that one are fit for shaving! [Rather,] actually, I can tell you [that the baraita refers to] the shaving of impurity; for once [the nazirite in a cemetery] has been sprinkled [on the third day] and repeated [on the seventh day] and immersed, he shaves on his seventh [day]. And that which [the baraita] poses [in contrast]: “His days of confirmed [leprosy], whose hair is not fit for shaving” — it was speaking of a shaving of naziriteship: For whereas [in the case of] a nazirite in a cemetery, when he shaves now, he shaves for naziriteship; a nazirite leper, however, when he shaves initially, shaves because he has healed from his leprosy. And this is what [the baraita] is teaching: If his days of confirmed [leprosy], which are not fit for a nazirite’s shaving of impurity, but rather for a shaving of leprosy, [do not count] — is it not all the more so that they do not count toward the tally of a naziriteship of purity? And [so] actually, I can tell you: Where one vowed naziriteship while in a cemetery, he requires a shaving of impurity.

Rashi on Nazir 18a:2:1.hebrew: תא שמע - ״וכי ימות מת עליו בפתע פתאום״ — בטהור שנטמא כו':
Rashi on Nazir 18a:2:1.english: Come and hear - “And if someone dies beside him suddenly, unexpectedly” — [the verse speaks] of a pure [nazirite] who became defiled, etc.

Rashi on Nazir 18a:2:2.english: A nazirite in a cemetery - [One] who was impure from the beginning of [his] naziriteship.

Rashi on Nazir 18a:3:1.hebrew: אינו דין כו' - מדקתני: ״ולפטור את הנזיר בקבר שאין טעון העברת שער״, שמע מינה דאין טעון גילוח שער — ש"מ:
Rashi on Nazir 18a:3:1.english: Is it not logical, etc. - From [the fact] that it teaches: “And to exempt the nazirite in a cemetery, that he does not require hair removal,” conclude from this that he does not require shaving of hair; [this is the meaning of] “learn from this.”

Rashi on Nazir 18a:5:1.hebrew: אלא טמא שנזר שביעי שלו - שטובל בו, עולה לו מן המנין, דהואיל ואינו בר קרבן, מתחיל למנות מבו ביום:
Rashi on Nazir 18a:5:1.english: Except that an impure person who took a vow of naziriteship, his seventh [day] - [The day] on which he immerses counts for him toward the tally [of his naziriteship], since, as he is not subject to [bringing] an offering, he begins counting from that very day.

Rashi on Nazir 18a:5:2.english: And [with regard to] a pure nazirite who became impure, his seventh [day] does not count for him as part of the tally - For he has no [complete] purification until the eighth day, when he brings his offerings, etc.

Rashi on Nazir 18a:7:1.hebrew: דתניא וקדש את ראשו - שיתחיל למנות לענין נזירות ביום הבאת קרבנותיו, שהוא שמיני, כדכתיב: "וביום השמיני יביא שתי תורים":
Rashi on Nazir 18a:7:1.english: As it is taught: “And he shall sanctify his head” - That he shall begin counting with regard to [his] naziriteship on the day of the bringing of his offerings, which is the eighth [day], as it is written: “And on the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves” (Numbers 6:10).

Rashi on Nazir 18a:7:2.hebrew: ביום תגלחתו - שהוא שביעי, כדכתיב: ״וגילח את ראשו ביום טהרתו ביום השביעי יגלחנו״:
Rashi on Nazir 18a:7:2.english: On the day of his shaving - Which is the seventh [day], as it is written: “And he shall shave his head on the day of his purification; on the seventh day he shall shave it.”

Rashi on Nazir 18a:8:1.hebrew: והא דתנן נזיר שנטמא כו' מאן תנא - חשיב להו טומאות הרבה, ואפ"ה לא מייתי עלייהו אלא קרבן אחד:
Rashi on Nazir 18a:8:1.english: And that which we learned: A nazirite who became impure, etc., who taught [it]? - [The mishna] considers them multiple impurities, and even so, he brings only one offering for them.

Rashi on Nazir 18a:8:2.hebrew: אמר רב חסדא ר' יוסי ברבי יהודה היא - דאמר: נזירות טהרה משביעי — שהוא יום תגלחתו — חיילא עילויה:
Rashi on Nazir 18a:8:2.english: Rav Ḥisda said: It is Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda - Who said [that] the naziriteship of purity takes effect upon him from the seventh [day] — which is the day of his shaving.

Rashi on Nazir 18a:8:3.english: And you find this - That there should be [a case of] “many impurities”.

Rashi on Nazir 18a:8:4.hebrew: כגון שנטמא - ומנה ששה כדי להזות עליה בשלישי ובשביעי, וחזר ונטמא ביו' ז' — דטומאה אחריתי איקרי, הואיל וטבל בו ביום; אבל בקרבן אינו חייב אלא אחד, שכל זמן שלא יצתה שעה שראויה להביא קרבן, שעדיין לא הגיע ליום ח', אינו חייב אלא קרבן אחד. אבל אם נטמא וחזר ונטמא בששי, אינו קורא לו טומאות הרבה, לפי שעדיין לא חל עליו טהרה כלל, ודמי לטומאה אריכתא. דאי אליבא דרבי, לא משכחת לה דמיקרי טומאות הרבה ולא ליחייב אלא קרבן אחד: דאי אמרת משכחת לה כגון שנטמא בשביעי וחזר ונטמא בשביעי, אינו חייב אלא קרבן אחד לסוף ימי טהרתו — כיון דנזירות דטהרה לא חיילא עליה עד יום שמיני, כולה חדא טומאה אריכתא היא, וליכא בהו טומאות הרבה. ואי אמרת כגון דנטמא בשמיני, והויין להו טומאות הרבה — הא נמי לא מיתרצתא דלא יביא אלא קרבן אחד; דאי אליבא דרבי, כיון דנטמא יום שמיני, שיצתה שעה שראויה להביא בה קרבן, נתחייב על כל אחד. הילכך, לא מיתוקמא אלא כרבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, ש"מ:
Rashi on Nazir 18a:8:4.english: For example, where he became impure - and he counted six [days] in order to be sprinkled on the third and on the seventh, and he then became impure again on the seventh day. For it is called another impurity, since he had immersed on that day; but regarding an offering, he is obligated [to bring] only one, because as long as a time fit to bring an offering has not passed — as he had not yet reached the eighth day — he is obligated [to bring] only one offering. However, if he became impure and then became impure again on the sixth [day], [the mishna] would not call it "many impurities," because purity had not taken effect upon him at all, and it is comparable to one extended impurity. For according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], you cannot find [a case where] it is called "many impurities" and yet he is obligated to bring only one offering: For if you were to say that you could find it [in a case] where he became impure on the seventh [day] and then became impure again on the seventh [day, and] he is obligated to bring only one offering at the end of his days of purification — since the naziriteship of purity does not take effect upon him until the eighth day, it is all one extended impurity, and there are not "many impurities" here. And if you were to say [that it is a case] where he became impure on the eighth [day], and thus they are "many impurities" — this too is not tenable [to say] that he should bring only one offering; for according to Rabbi, once he became impure on the eighth day, when a time fit to bring an offering in it had passed, he became obligated for each and every one. Therefore, it can only be established in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda. Conclude from this [that it is so].

Tosafot on Nazir 18a:10:1.hebrew: דכתיב מאשר חטא על הנפש - וכתיב בההוא קרא לאלתר: "וקדש ראשו ביום ההוא", פי': ביום שכיפר עליו, דהיינו בשמיני:
Tosafot on Nazir 18a:10:1.english: As it is written: “For he sinned by the soul” - And it is written in that same verse immediately: “And he shall sanctify his head on that day,” meaning: on the day that he made atonement for him, which is on the eighth [day].

Tosafot on Nazir 18a:10:2.hebrew: אם כן לימא קרא וקדש את ראשו - ופשיטא דאשמיני דקיימינן ביה איירי; "ביום ההוא" למה לי? אם אינו ענין לשמיני, תנהו לשביעי, דאייתור למשדי אשביעי:
Tosafot on Nazir 18a:10:2.english: “If so, let the verse state: ‘And he shall sanctify his head’” - And it would be obvious that it is speaking of the eighth [day], which we are dealing with; [so] why do I need “on that day”? If it is not needed for the eighth [day], apply it to the seventh [day], as it is superfluous [and available] to apply to the seventh [day].

Tosafot on Nazir 18a:1:1.hebrew: ימי חלוטו מי לא בעי תגלחת - בסוף ימי חלוטו, כדכתיב: "וכבס המטהר את בגדיו וגלח את כל שערו". אבל תגלחת דטהרה לית ביה במצורע, דגם תגלחת שניה שמגלח אחר ימי ספרו — מתוך טומאה הוא מגלחה, שגם בימי ספרו מטמא אדם במגע:
Tosafot on Nazir 18a:1:1.english: "Do the days of his confirmed leprosy not require shaving?" - [Meaning,] at the end of the days of his confirmed leprosy, as it is written: "And he who is being cleansed shall wash his clothes, and shave off all his hair" (Leviticus 14:8). But a shaving of purity does not exist for a leper, for even the second shaving, which he shaves after the days of his counting, he shaves [it] from [a state of] impurity, since even during the days of his counting he defiles a person through contact.

Tosafot on Nazir 18a:1:2.hebrew: לא תגלחת טומאה דנזירות קתני - כלומר: לעולם אימא לך תגלחת דטומאה. ודקאמרת דבימי חלוטו נמי איכא תגלחת דטומאה — לא, תגלחת דנזירות קתני: דנזיר בקבר ראוי שערו לתגלחת מחמת נזירות, ובימי חלוטו לא בעי תגלחת דטומאה מחמת נזירות אלא מחמת צרעתו, וזה אין שייך לנזירות כלל; הילכך, לא יעלו לו ימיו לנזירותו:
Tosafot on Nazir 18a:1:2.english: "No, it is teaching [about] the shaving of impurity of naziriteship" - That is to say: Actually, I can say to you [that the baraita is referring to] the shaving of impurity; and as for that which you said, that during his days of confirmed leprosy there is also a shaving of impurity — "No, it is teaching [about] the shaving of naziriteship": for [in the case of] a nazirite in a cemetery, his hair is fit for shaving on account of naziriteship, whereas during his days of confirmed leprosy he does not require a shaving of impurity on account of naziriteship, but rather on account of his leprosy, and this does not pertain to naziriteship at all; therefore, his days do not count toward his naziriteship.

Tosafot on Nazir 18a:2:1.hebrew: בטהור שנטמא הכתוב מדבר - כלומר, שהתחיל למנות נזירות בטהרה ואחרי כן נטמא, כדכתיב: "והימים הראשונים יפלו":
Tosafot on Nazir 18a:2:1.english: "The verse is speaking of a ritually pure [nazirite] who became impure" - That is to say, [one] who began counting naziriteship in ritual purity, and afterward became impure, as it is written: "And the former days shall be void" (Numbers 6:12).

Tosafot on Nazir 18a:2:2.hebrew: ולפטור את הנזיר בקבר שאין טעון העברת שיער והבאת ציפרים - והוא הדין דממעט ליה מאשם, דכתיב בההוא עניינא. והיינו דקאמר במתני' בנזיר בקבר: "אינו מביא קרבן טומאה" — דמיעטיה קרא, כדדרשינן הכא:
Tosafot on Nazir 18a:2:2.english: "And to exempt the nazirite in a cemetery, that he does not require hair removal and the bringing of birds" - And the same law applies that [the verse] excludes him from a guilt offering, which is written in that passage. And that is what [the Mishnah] says regarding a nazirite in a cemetery: "He does not bring an offering of impurity" — for the verse excluded him, as we expound here.

Tosafot on Nazir 18a:3:1.hebrew: והלא דברים ק"ו - פירוש: אי לא מיעטיה קרא, "ומה טהור שנטמא טעון כו'" — כלומר, שטומאתו הזקיקתו לכך; כל שכן היכא דנטמא מתחילתו, שטמא ביותר, שהזקיקתו טומאתו לכל! ת"ל: "וטמא ראש נזרו" — מיותר, דמצי למימר: "וכי ימות מת [עליו] בפתע פתאום וגלח ראשו":
Tosafot on Nazir 18a:3:1.english: "And are these matters not an a fortiori inference?" - Explanation: If the verse had not excluded him, [one would have argued:] "Just as one who was pure and became defiled requires [hair removal and the bringing of birds]..." — that is, his defilement obligated him in this; all the more so in a case where he was defiled from the outset, where he is more severely defiled, that his defilement should obligate him in all [of this]! [Therefore,] the verse states: "And he defiles his consecrated head" — [which is] superfluous, as it could have said: "And if someone dies [upon him] suddenly, unawares, then he shall shave his head."

Tosafot on Nazir 18a:7:1.hebrew: ביום הבאת קרבנותיו - דכך כתיב בקרא: "ביום השמיני יביא שתי תורים וכו' וכפר עליו מאשר חטא על הנפש וקדש ראשו ביום ההוא" — שמעינן: ביום שמיני, שהוא הבאת קרבנותיו, כדמפרש לקמן בסמוך:
Tosafot on Nazir 18a:7:1.english: "On the day of the bringing of his offerings" - For so it is written in the verse: "On the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves, etc., and make atonement for him for that he sinned by reason of the dead, and he shall sanctify his head on that day" — we learn: on the eighth day, which is [the day of] the bringing of his offerings, as [the Gemara] explains immediately below.

Tosafot on Nazir 18a:7:2.hebrew: ביום תגלחתו - הכתוב מדבר, דהיינו בשביעי. בסמוך מפרש טעמא:
Tosafot on Nazir 18a:7:2.english: "On the day of his shaving" - Scripture is speaking [of this], that is, on the seventh [day]. Nearby, [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Tosafot on Nazir 18a:8:1.hebrew: והא דתנן - פ' קמא דכריתות (דף ט.):
Tosafot on Nazir 18a:8:1.english: "And that which we learned" - [This is in] the first chapter of Keritot (9a).

Tosafot on Nazir 18a:8:2.hebrew: משביעי הוא דחיילא - משביעי — שמתחיל לימנות נזירות משביעי:
Tosafot on Nazir 18a:8:2.english: "It is from the seventh that it takes effect" - From the seventh — that he begins to count the naziriteship from the seventh [day].

Tosafot on Nazir 18a:8:3.hebrew: ומשכחת טומאות הרבה כגון שנטמא ביום שביעי וחזר ונטמא בשביעי - לסוף שביעי, אחר שהזה ושנה וטבל; דמיד כשהזה וטבל, חל עליו באותו יום נזירות טהרה, שיום שביעי הוי ממנין שלשים. כי נטמא ביום שביעי, כיון דחל עליה נזירות טהרה כבר, חשיב ליה טומאה אחריתי; ולא הוה כנטמא בששי, דההיא ודאי טומאה אריכתא היא, דאכתי לא חל עליה נזירות טהרה. ומכל מקום פוטר עצמו מקרבן טומאה אחר, כיון שנטמא בשביעי ולא יצא שעה אחת ליום שראוי הוא להביא קרבנות, דהיינו ביום שמיני:
Tosafot on Nazir 18a:8:3.english: "And you find [a case of] multiple impurities, such as where he became impure on the seventh day and again became impure on the seventh day" - [This means] at the end of the seventh [day], after he was sprinkled upon [on the third day], repeated [the sprinkling on the seventh day], and immersed. For immediately when he was sprinkled upon and immersed, the naziriteship of purity took effect upon him on that day, as the seventh day is [counted] from the tally of thirty [days]. When he became impure on the seventh day, since the naziriteship of purity had already taken effect upon him, it is considered for him a distinct impurity, and it is not like [one who] became impure on the sixth [day], which is certainly a prolonged impurity, as the naziriteship of purity had not yet taken effect upon him. And nevertheless, he exempts himself from another offering of impurity, since he became impure on the seventh [day] and not a single hour had elapsed into a day on which he is fit to bring offerings, that is, on the eighth day.

Tosafot on Nazir 18a:9:1.hebrew: דאי רבי - דאמר דאינו מתחיל למנות נזירות טהרה עד יום שמיני — כולה טומאה אריכתא היא, דלא נראה עדיין להתחיל נזירות, והוי כאילו נטמא בששי; ואמאי קרי ליה "טומאות הרבה"? "ואי דנטמא בשמיני" כו' — כיון דיצא לשעה שראוי להביא קרבנותיו, והוי כנטמא אחר הבאת קרבנותיו, דודאי צריך להביא קרבן טומאה אחר:
Tosafot on Nazir 18a:9:1.english: For if [it follows] Rabbi - [As Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi] says that he does not begin counting [his] naziriteship of purity until the eighth day — it is all [one] long ritual impurity, for he was not yet fit to begin [his] naziriteship, and it is as though he became ritually impure on the sixth [day]; why [then] does [the Mishnah] call it "many impurities"? "And if [it is a case] where he became ritually impure on the eighth [day]," etc. — since he has reached a time that is fit to bring his offerings, it is as though he became ritually impure after bringing his offerings, for he certainly must bring another offering for ritual impurity.
